data.title: Ponická Huta – Na kláštore, a hillfort of copper miners
data.excerpt: The hillfort of Na kláštore on the western ridge of the Učovník massif is girdled by rampart defences some 400 m long, most massive on the eastern side. The quality of the finds and the proximity of the copper deposits at Drienok suggest that its inhabitants were responsible for mining and working copper, and the most remarkable find from the site is a bronze figurine of a naked man.

children.text: The site of the hillfort of Na Kláštore lies in the Ponická hill country on the western ridge of the Učovník massif (759 m above sea level). The summit of the hill is separated by the valleys of the Zolná stream on the northern side and the Malá Zolná stream on the southern side. To the west the two streams merge.

The hillfort lies about 500 m east of their confluence. The average elevation is 565.00 – 574.00 m above sea level. The northern and southern slopes fall steeply away into the valley. The western ridge ends in a rocky crag, in the direction of the locality of Baby. The original approach to the hillfort is from the southern side of the valley through which the Malá Zolná stream flows.

To this day the traces of a serpentine road are clearly visible in the field, opening out in the western part of the fortified enclosure of the hillfort. The rampart defences are most massive on the eastern side and their approximate length is 400 m. The quality of the finds, the proximity of the copper deposits at the locality of Drienok (4 km to the north-east), the iron deposits, as well as the fortification of the enclosure demonstrate that the hillfort of Na Kláštore must have had at least regional importance. The earliest occupation of the hillfort belongs to the period of the Lusatian culture. Karol Pieta dates the hillfort to the so-called pre-Púchov stage (stage C) of the La Tène period (the close of the Late Iron Age). It is above all the iron hoard that was found, and in it the so-called Dürrnberg-type small chisel, that belongs to this period. The later period (C2) is in turn dated by brooches of composite construction. Iron spearheads were also found here. In this period we also record intensive iron working here. The most interesting find is a bronze figurine of a naked man, which ranks among the important finds in the whole of Slovakia.

children.text:
Besides the mining and working of ores, it is likely that the hillfort also played a guard role beside the road passing out of the Zolná valley, along which a road led to the sites in the surroundings of Zvolen and into the area of the Ľubietová mining district, with its important copper deposits as well as finds of the Late Bronze Age. Important roads of supra-regional character led across this territory, by which copper was distributed to its final customers. 
 
 It is assumed that the population of this hillfort was responsible for the mining and working of copper from the local deposit, and held an important position within the communication routes of exchange trade. The fortification around the whole enclosure of the hillfort also suggests that it was not merely defensive in character, but also functioned as a store for copper semi-finished products. From this follows the essential fact that this type of hillfort must have been the result of the organised work of a larger group of people. The proof of this is the richly represented table pottery (cups, bowls), the quality of its manufacture (smoothed, burnished surface) and its rich ornamentation.
